svg.title: One Semantic Layer, Shared by BI and AI
svg.desc: An architecture diagram in three lanes. OneLake data stores (lakehouse and warehouse Delta tables) feed a semantic model built in Direct Lake mode. The model layer adds endorsed measures, row-level security, and framing control. A Fabric IQ ontology sits alongside the model, mapping business concepts onto it without moving data. From there, four consumption surfaces read the same governed layer: Power BI reports, Analyze in Excel, Copilot, and a Fabric data agent. A warning node calls out the Direct Lake framing lag as a freshness limit every consumer inherits.
svg.text: Enterprise semantic layer on Microsoft Fabric

g.title: Lakehouse Delta tables — Spark-managed gold tables in OneLake, stored as Delta.
g.text: One governed set of Delta tables in OneLake, served through shared certified semantic models, consumed by both BI and AI.

g.title: Warehouse Delta tables — T-SQL-managed star schema tables, also stored as Delta in OneLake.
Direct Lake freshness is framing-bound — Every consumer reads data as of the last framing operation, not the live table.
